title: Application-Dependent Cipher/FHE Selection
summary: The designs may become more alike under converging modulus choices, but the best cipher/FHE pairing for each application range remains undetermined.

formal_statement.body: Among FHE-friendly symmetric ciphers, Elisabeth instantiated with larger moduli $q$ and HERA-like or PASTA-like designs instantiated with smaller moduli may become increasingly similar. Determine which cipher---and ultimately which symmetric-cipher/FHE combination---delivers the best global performance for each range of applications, taking into account the data processing required for the intended homomorphic operations.

scope.domain: Application-dependent performance optimization of FHE-friendly symmetric ciphers for hybrid homomorphic encryption.
parameters: q: modulus for Elisabeth, with larger values compared against smaller-modulus HERA-like or PASTA-like designs
application range: context for comparing global performance and required homomorphic data processing
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine which cipher and symmetric-cipher/FHE combination achieves the best global performance for each application range while accounting for the data processing required by the intended homomorphic operations.

citations.label: Towards Case-Optimized Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption -Featuring the Elisabeth Stream Cipher-

progress.summary: The source observes that larger-modulus Elisabeth instances and smaller-modulus HERA-/PASTA-like ciphers may become increasingly similar. It explicitly frames application-dependent cipher choice as a long-term problem evaluated through global performance and homomorphic data-processing needs.
citation_labels: Orel Cosseron et al., Towards Case-Optimized Hybrid Homomorphic Encryption -Featuring the Elisabeth Stream Cipher-
